newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 18.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- The Irish government and opposition parties have welcomed the British government's decision to reject plans by UK Nirex Limited for a 1.8 billion sterling nuclear waste dump at Sellafield.

- Differences between the Irish and British governments over the setting of a date for the entry of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, into multi-party talks when they resume in June have emerged clearly during the Irish Prime Minister's visit to Washington.
- The Irish pound has closed above 98 pence against sterling for the first time since February 5, at 98.10 from 97.70 at Friday's close.
- Irish taxpayers face legal costs of up to 150 million Irish pounds in army "hearing damage" cases it emerged on Monday.
- A number of top civil servants are in line for tax-free golden handshakes of 120,000 Irish pounds each.
- The U.S. government on Monday tacitly threw its weight behind the push to make President Mary Robinson the next UN High Commisioner for Human Rights.

- Irish businesses who have joined the 'Shop Ireland' and 'Ireland at Home' Internet shopping service will have to overcome a major cost barrier because access to the Internet from Ireland is over three times more expensive than in North America.
- The White House on Monday gave early indications that it will push to get Ireland's President Mary Robinson appointed to a top United Nations human rights post.
- Irish farmers on Monday threatened a national revolt over fears that dairy incomes would plummet by 25 percent this year, with retail milk prices already dropping by one Irish pence per litre.
